venue.name: Metchosin Schoolhouse Museum
venue.description: The Metchosin Schoolhouse Museum is housed in the one room schoolhouse that opened in spring 1872, the first school building opened in British Columbia after Confederation. It is run by the volunteer Metchosin Museum Society, which also runs the Metchosin Pioneer Museum a short distance along the same road. The displays inside are all about the teaching and learning that went on in the schoolhouse. The building was restored over three years from 2019 and a lift was added, and admission is free with donations welcome.

facility_notes.washrooms: The groups may have a snack and/or lunch, washroom break, and then visit the other museum.
facility_notes.lunch_space: The groups may have a snack and/or lunch, washroom break, and then visit the other museum.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: The Schoolhouse Museum is fully wheelchair accessible. Maximum occupancy is 12 visitors.

venue.hours_notes: Saturdays 1 pm to 4 pm and Sundays 11 am to 3 pm. All locations are closed on statutory holidays.

programs.name: School Field Trip by Appointment
programs.description: Museum curators run a planned lesson pitched at the grade level. Half the class starts in the Schoolhouse Museum while the other half tours the Pioneer Museum along the road, then the two halves swap after a snack and a washroom break. The site says each museum takes 30, 45 or 60 minutes depending on the grade. The price is five dollars per student and the visit is booked through an inquiry form.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in the one room schoolhouse and do an appropriate lesson for their grade, write in cursive with a dip pen and ink, spin a button spinner, and hunt for artifacts among the displays.
programs.our_note: The visit is built around splitting a class in two, so half your group is at the Pioneer Museum along the road while the other half is in the schoolhouse. Only Thursdays and Fridays are offered and only from September to June, so ask early. The length changes with the grade, so say how old your group is when you send the form.
programs.practical_summary: A washroom break and a snack or lunch are built into the visit, and the schoolhouse is fully wheelchair accessible. Bus parking, how many adults have to come and the youngest age they take are not stated, so ask when you book.
programs.evidence: Cost: F i v e d o l l a r s/student

programs.name: Small Group Tour by Appointment
programs.description: Museum curators show small groups what it was like to attend the Metchosin Schoolhouse between 1872 and 1914. Visitors use a dip pen for cursive writing, get instruction on how to work a button spinner, and have the museum displays interpreted for them. The schoolhouse holds 12 visitors at a time. The Pioneer Museum along the road can be seen the same day or booked separately, and the site says a second day carries a cost without saying how much.
programs.what_children_do: Gather in one small room, try writing with a dip pen and ink, work a button spinner on a string, and listen while a curator explains the displays.
programs.our_note: Twelve visitors at a time is the ceiling here, so a full class will not fit in one go and this suits a small group. Booking is by inquiry form only, with no phone number or email on the site. Ask what a second day at the Pioneer Museum costs if you want both.
programs.practical_summary: The schoolhouse is fully wheelchair accessible and holds 12 visitors at a time. No price is published for a small group tour and the months it runs are not stated, so it is worth asking.
programs.evidence: The Schoolhouse Museum is fully wheelchair accessible. Maximum occupancy is 12 visitors.

images.alt: A small white clapboard schoolhouse behind a white picket fence, with a bare tree and a wooden arbour in front of it.
A white panelled museum room with glass display cabinets, wooden desks and framed black and white class photographs on the wall.
Children sitting at rows of wooden school desks in a white panelled room, holding strings stretched between their hands.
A child seated at a small antique reed organ, below a wall of framed documents and an old group photograph.
